items.title: Mike De Lay Interview, 1958-09-02
items.q: Then I began taking lessons with Manuel Perez. He was my first teacher.

ctx.x: Can you tell about your parents? Did they play instruments?

My mother was a pianist. She was a very good pianist, but not professionally. She didn't play professionally. And she wanted me to play violin, but I never did like violin. And what made me like trumpet or cornet, as I might say, was Manuel Perez. Manuel Perez's sister, she's the only one that's living today. Her name is Lilia Perez. She's my godmother.
Do you know where she's living about?

items.title: Mike De Lay Interview, 1970-11-14
items.q: before Ludd, John Tron came along, I was crazy about my teacher, Manuel Perez.

ctx.x: Mike, when you were playing up, do you consider the best cornet player?

Oh, that's a kind of hard thing. Sure. To say, because you know the reason why, when I was a kid, you're talking about it? Yeah. Because I was listening to the cornet and trumpets all my, what's that cornet then, that damn night. All my days, I just loved it. My mother wouldn't buy me one. She wouldn't buy me a violin. I didn't want to buy me. But anyway, I had my, well, before Ludd, John Tron came along, I was crazy about my teacher, Manuel Perez. He had such a name around there, you know, around him. He, when…
I said, plenty gold on the lawn socks. No, I didn't know.

items.title: Mike De Lay Interview, 1970-11-14
items.q: I did know one thing about Lerz. I remember when I first, I don't recall the year, but I remember when I first thought, yeah, Lerz in the street, Perez. And, boy, we'd be, this is no joke. I think about the few books I read about. How they got a lot of truth in this, because it went for me. Because

ctx.x: And he played Confession. Huh? Wait a minute. Wait a minute. See if I can. Roughly. Well, I can roughly. I can really roughly get it for you. Pretty close. No kidding. Anywhere between, uh, anyway, I'm not sure, but I would say any time between 29, 39 and 41. Of course, no later than about me of 41. No, no, no, I'm wrong. No later than March of 41, because April of 41 I was in a service. So, yeah, it would be about that. I'll never forget that he played competitive. He thanked me for letting me play at the hall,…
Okay, push it off. This thing about Bonk, John and I, is kind of a private argument because, uh...
